title: Welcome to PlanetMusic: Your Personal Vault
summary: A quick intro to your personal music library, and why everything stays in your own browser.
content:
Everyone listens to music differently. That's why I built PlanetMusic as a personal, customizable music player and lyrics app that keeps everything in your own browser.

Unlike cloud services, your saved songs and settings stay on your own device.

---

## 1. The Cosmos and the Vault

When you use the search bar, PlanetMusic pulls results from the **Cosmos**, which is how PlanetMusic connects to the public iTunes and Deezer music catalogs. When you find a track you like, click **Add to Vault** in the player modal.

Once a song is in your Vault, it's saved in your browser. From there you can edit its info, give artists high-resolution images, upload local MP3s, or rewrite the lyrics completely.

> **PRO TIP:** Since everything is saved on your device, export a JSON backup of your Vault every now and then. The download icon in the top right corner does it. The backup covers your text data (lyrics, timings, settings), not your uploaded MP3s, so back up often.

## 2. No accounts

There are no usernames, passwords, or cloud accounts. Just start searching the Cosmos and build your library.

title: How Player Audio Streams & Custom Links Work
summary: How to choose your audio source, match the right track length, and fix Deezer links.
content:
The player plays audio alongside your synced lyrics. The audio can come from YouTube, Deezer, or a file on your own device.

This post covers how to set up your audio.

---

## 1. Playback controls

* **Play / Pause:** Click the button on the bottom player bar or the control panel.
* **Spacebar:** Press it at any time to toggle playback.
* **Progress bar:** Click anywhere along it to jump to that part of the song.

---

## 2. Choosing a source

In the **Play Music From** section of the song panel, you'll find a row of buttons, one for each audio source. Pick a source there, and click a different one whenever you want to switch.

You can paste YouTube Music URLs and full Deezer web addresses as links.

---

## 3. Local audio files

You can also play audio from a file on your device. Supported formats are `.mp3`, `.wav`, and `.m4a`. Local files start playing immediately, with no network buffering.

---

## 4. Match the song duration

Before you pick or paste an audio source, check the **Duration** in the track details at the top of the song panel.

> **CHECK THE DURATION:** The track length is listed under **Duration** in the track details. Pick audio that matches it.

Songs often come in several versions, so choose a file or link with the **exact same length as the Duration shown**. If your audio is shorter or longer, your line timestamps will drift out of sync with the music.

---

## 5. Formatting Deezer links

The mobile and desktop share links from Deezer **won't work** in the player. They're shortened share links, not full web addresses.

> **CRITICAL DEEZER WORKFLOW:** Open the shortened share link in a browser tab first to get the full web address, then paste that instead.

### Step by step

1. In Deezer, click **Share** on the song and choose **Copy Link**.
2. Open a new browser tab, paste the share link into the address bar, and press **Enter**.
3. Wait a second for the page to finish loading so the full address shows up.
4. Copy that full URL from the address bar and paste it into the player field.

title: Formatting Lyrics & Singer Tags
summary: How to tag singers in section headers, use text styles to assign up to four artists, and get automatic colors in the preview.
content:
Formatting your lyrics tells PlanetMusic which artist is singing each phrase, so the preview window can give every singer their own color.

This post covers section headers, text styles, and pasting lyrics from online sources.

---

## 1. Section headers with multiple artists

Put up to **four artists** in square brackets after a colon. Each one gets their own text style:

`[Verse: Artist 1, _Artist 2_, **Artist 3**, **_Artist 4_**]`

> **COLON RULE:** Only the text **after the colon** is read as artist names. Anything before the colon is ignored. If there's no colon, like `[Verse 1]`, the section **defaults to the primary track artist**.

---

## 2. The four text styles

The styles are mapped to artists in real time:

1. **Plain Text** = Artist 1
2. **_Italics_** = Artist 2
3. **Bold** = Artist 3
4. **_Bold-Italics_** = Artist 4

### Example

```text
[Verse: Artist 1, _Artist 2_, **Artist 3**, **_Artist 4_**]
Artist 1 sings this plain line, _(Artist 2 sings this italic adlib)_
**Artist 3 sings this bold line**, **_Artist 4 sings this bold-italic line_**
```

---

## 3. Multiline styling and pasting lyrics

You don't have to format everything from scratch.

* **Pasting from online sources:** Lyrics copied from sites like Genius or AZLyrics often come with italics for background vocals or bold text for featured artists. When you paste them into the editor, those styles are mapped to Artist 2, 3, or 4 based on your header.
* **Multiline styling:** Formatting works across several lines at once. Wrap five lines in a row in `_italics_` or `**bold**` and that whole block goes to the matching artist.

---

## 4. Check the live preview

Keep an eye on the **Live Preview Window** while you type or paste:

* **Colors:** Each of the four text styles gets its own artist theme color right away.
* **Layout:** Lines show up with their assigned weights, colors, and split layouts as you go, so you can check who's singing what before you save.

title: How to Search and Save Songs to Your Vault
summary: How to search your Vault and the Cosmos, and how to save songs to your library.
content:
Finding music and adding it to your collection only takes a few clicks. You can filter the songs you've already saved, or search online databases for new ones.

---

## 1. Searching your Vault

The search bar at the top of your dashboard filters your saved collection as you type.

* **Instant filtering:** Start typing an artist name, song title, or keyword and your local cards filter immediately.
* **Resetting your view:** Click **Home** in the top navigation bar to clear your search and go back to your full collection.

---

## 2. Searching the Cosmos

If a track isn't in your collection, use **Cosmos Search** to look through online music databases.

1. Type the song title or artist name into the main search box.
2. Press **Enter** on your keyboard or click the **Search Icon** button.
3. Your view splits into **Vault** results and **Cosmos** results.
4. Matches from public databases show up in the Cosmos column.

When the same track turns up in different databases, the duplicates are merged, which keeps the results easy to scan.

---

## 3. Adding a song to your Vault

Once you find the song you want, open it by clicking its song card, then click **Add to Vault** at the bottom of the left control panel.

> **QUICK TIP:** Adding a track automatically fetches any available online lyrics and timing files, so the song is ready to play right away.

---

## 4. Where saved songs go

Every saved track is saved in your browser, on your own device.

* **Home dashboard:** Saved songs show up on your **main home dashboard**.
* **Instant loading:** Tracks in your **Vault** load right away, with no new search needed.

title: How to Sync Songs with Music
summary: How to map line timestamps, use the keyboard shortcuts, split and loop ad-libs, and switch audio sources.
content:
Syncing is what makes your lyrics scroll and highlight in time with the music. How smooth it looks in playback depends on when you press the start and end markers.

Here's how the sync workspace works.

---

## 1. Keyboard shortcuts

Use these while the song plays:

* **`Spacebar`**: Plays or pauses the audio.
* **`Down Arrow`**: Tap once to set the **Start** marker. Tap again to set the **End** marker and jump to the next line.
* **`Up Arrow`**: Clears the current line's timing and steps back to the previous line.
* **`Left` / `Right` Arrows**: Nudge the audio backward or forward by **1 second**.

---

## 2. Splitting and syncing ad-libs

Background vocals, echoes, and chants in parentheses `(like this)` can be pulled out on their own by clicking **Split Adlibs**.

> **CRITICAL RULE:** An ad-lib's timestamps live inside its parent line. An ad-lib **can't extend past the end timestamp** of its main line.

Four rules to follow when you sync ad-libs:

1. **Sync the main line first.** Map the main sentence before you touch the ad-lib.
2. **Click ad-lib lines manually.** Normal line-by-line syncing with `Down Arrow` **skips ad-lib lines entirely**, so you have to click an ad-lib line yourself to select and sync it.
3. **Parent looping is automatic.** Clicking an unsynced ad-lib line **loops the audio** between the start and end markers of its main line.
4. **There's a shortcut for the ending.** Click the ad-lib line and tap `Down Arrow` **once** when the echo starts, then let the song play. When playback reaches the end of the main line, the ad-lib automatically gets that same end marker.

---

## 3. Auto-Sync and database mapping

You can save time by pulling pre-timed files from open databases:

* **Auto-Sync Lyrics:** Searches online libraries and fetches fully timed lyrics for you.
* **Map Timings from Auto:** Copies the time markers from public databases onto lyrics you typed yourself.

---

## 4. Switching audio sources

Different audio files can play at slightly different speeds or start at different points. If your timing feels off, try another source.

> **QUICK TIP:** Click the **Source Badge Name** (YouTube, Deezer, or Local MP3) in the top bar to cycle through the available audio feeds.

title: How Ad-libs Find Their Spot in Focused View
summary: How Focused View finds a clear spot for background vocals, and how it arranges big groups of singers.
content:
**Focused View** is one of the more interesting ways to watch lyrics in PlanetMusic. You can pick it under **Lyrics View Modes** on the song panel, next to Live and Plain Text.

Live View scrolls vertically like traditional karaoke. Focused View puts the main lyric right in the center of the screen instead. Background vocals and echoes get their own timing and their own place on the screen, so they never sit on top of the main line.

---

## 1. How ad-libs find their spot

When a secondary artist sings an ad-lib, PlanetMusic has to decide where on the screen to put it.

First it works out how much room is taken up by the main lyric, the artist name in the background, and the edges of the screen. Then it looks for the biggest open area that's left and places the ad-lib there, so it never lands on top of anything.

## 2. Songs with lots of singers

If a song has a big group singing at once, the screen is divided into a grid and every singer gets their own spot in it. For five singers, for example, the grid is five across and two down.

The singers aren't placed in the same order on every row. The top row goes `1 2 3 4 5`, and the bottom row shifts to `2 3 4 5 1`. That way singers aren't stacked directly on top of each other, and nothing overlaps.

title: How to Use the Translation Workspace
summary: Translate lyrics, tweak pronunciation and CJK spacing, then save or export your draft.
content:
The translation workspace is where you translate lyrics, fix pronunciation, and set up spacing for Japanese or Chinese, all in one place. Nothing is applied to your song until you save, so you can review everything first.

---

## 1. Opening the workspace

Open a song that has lyrics and choose **Edit Translation**. Each row shows the original lyric, a language tag, the pronunciation when there is one, and an English translation field. Japanese (`ja`) and Chinese (`zh...`) rows also get a spacing field. Split ad-libs show up as indented rows.

The language tag starts as `auto`. If detection gets it wrong, set a code yourself, like `ko`, `ja`, `zh-CN`, `es`, or `en`. `en` means the source is already English, so the translation and pronunciation are cleared for that row.

---

## 2. Translating lines

Pick whichever method suits the lyric:

* **Translate All** translates every row using its language tag, then fills in the translation and pronunciation where they're available. While it runs, the button turns into **Stop Translation**.
* **Translate with Context** groups rows by language and translates each group together, which helps keep the surrounding meaning. The lines around a lyric matter a lot for accuracy, especially with poetry.
* **Refresh a line** with the circular-arrow button on that row to fetch a new result for just that row.

Translation always targets English. Before you save, check names, slang, wordplay, and line breaks.

---

## 3. Spacing Japanese and Chinese

For rows tagged `ja` or `zh...`, you can edit the **Spacing Field** by hand or click **Auto Spacing**. Auto Spacing estimates where the word breaks go, keeps punctuation, and updates pronunciation, but only for the matching rows. It can take longer than translation, since it works through each line piece by piece.

Treat the result as a first draft. Check names, particles, mixed Latin text, and punctuation. Keep in mind that once a row has a spacing value, later translations of that row use it.

---

## 4. Editing, importing, and exporting

You can edit the translation and pronunciation directly. **Export Text** downloads one block per row, with a blank line between blocks.

**Import Text** matches each block to a row by its original lyric, ignoring case. If a lyric doesn't match, it falls back to the block's position, so keep your blocks in order.

---

## 5. Saving or resetting

* **Save Changes** applies the draft to the song in your Vault and closes the workspace.
* **Cancel** asks before throwing away unsaved edits.
* **Refresh Lyrics** clears translations, pronunciation, and spacing, and resets the language tags to `auto`. Your original lyrics stay as they are.

title: Auto Spacing for Japanese & Chinese Lyrics
summary: What Auto Spacing does for Japanese and Chinese lyrics, how to use it, and how it works out where the spaces go.
content:
Japanese and Chinese don't put spaces between words. That's fine for reading, but a karaoke-style player works best when it knows where each word starts and ends, so it can highlight words in time with the music.

**Auto Spacing** adds those spaces for you.

---

## 1. What it does

Auto Spacing looks at a Japanese or Chinese line and puts spaces between the words. For example, `君の声が聞こえる` becomes `君の 声が 聞こえる`. It keeps the punctuation and updates the pronunciation for those rows too.

## 2. How to use it

1. Open a song that has lyrics and choose **Edit Translation**.
2. Spacing fields appear on Japanese (`ja`) and Chinese (`zh...`) rows. If a row isn't detected correctly, set its language tag yourself.
3. Click **Auto Spacing**.
4. Check the results in the spacing fields, and fix anything by hand.
5. Click **Save Changes**.

## 3. How it works out where the spaces go

Here's what happens, step by step.

**The problem.** When a Japanese line like `君の声が聞こえる` is translated, you get its pronunciation written in English letters, like `Kimi no koe ga kikoeru`. That already has spaces in it, but it doesn't say which Japanese characters belong to which word.

**The workaround.** PlanetMusic works through the line one piece at a time, starting from the end and moving toward the beginning, and works out how each piece sounds. There's a catch: a character on its own is often pronounced differently than it is inside a sentence. So each piece is always read with the rest of the line around it, and only that one piece's sound is picked out. For example, it reads the whole line and pulls out just how `る` sounds in that context.

**The matching.** Once it knows how every piece sounds in context, it lines those sounds up against the full pronunciation. Wherever a piece ends exactly where a space falls in the pronunciation, a space goes into the original text. This takes a few seconds, which is why Auto Spacing can take longer than translation.

## 4. Double-check the result

Treat the result as a first draft. Check names, particles, mixed Latin text, and punctuation before you save.

title: The Image Manager: Customizing Artist Profiles
summary: How to set persistent high-resolution images and distinct colors for every artist in your Vault.
content:
In Live and Focused lyrics view, the background crossfades between artist photos depending on who's singing at that moment.

By default, the app fetches artist images from Wikipedia. Sometimes Wikipedia doesn't have a great photo, or you'd rather use the look of a specific era. That's what the **Image Manager** is for.

---

## 1. Opening the Image Manager

Open any saved song in your Vault that has lyrics and click **Manage Artists** on the left panel.

You'll see a list of every singer detected in your lyrics, based on your section headers and ad-lib tags.

## 2. Setting images and colors

* **Image URLs:** Paste a direct image link (one ending in .jpg, .png, and so on) into the artist's text field. A URL is all it needs. High-definition square images work best.
* **Artist Colors:** Click the color swatch next to an artist's name to give them their own text color.

Images and colors apply globally. If you set an image for an artist in one song, that same image and color gets used in *every* song in your Vault that features them. You only have to do it once.

## 3. Finding good images

Clicking an artist's name in the manager opens a DuckDuckGo image search for high-resolution square images. Right-click an image you like, choose "Copy Image Address", and paste it into the app.

title: Personalizing the Viewing Experience & Layout
summary: Adjust the typography, background opacity, and layout proportions in the Settings tab.
content:
PlanetMusic is meant to look good on a huge desktop monitor and on a small phone screen. You can tune almost every part of how it looks in the **Settings Tab**.

---

## 1. Typography controls

The typography settings cover everything from the main lyrics down to the phonetic transliterations. Between the font sizes and the background opacity, you control how legible everything is.

* **Live Font Size:** Scales the main text in the scrolling view.
* **Floating Adlib Size:** Sets how large the background vocals appear when they orbit the main text in Focused View.
* **Translation Spacing:** Sliders that push the English translation higher above the text and the Romaji pronunciation lower below it, so the lines have room to breathe.

## 2. Layout proportions

You can change the width of the song cards on the home screen, the padding inside them, and whether their corners are sharp or rounded.

If you'd like the lyrics to take up more of the screen than the album art, adjust the **Modal Split Ratio** slider.

## 3. Ambient View

If you just want music playing on a second monitor, go to Settings and click **Enter Ambient View**. It hides the whole track grid and the search bar, leaving only floating chat-bubble lyrics that rise from the bottom of the screen while the music plays.

title: Data Storage, Backups & The Purge Button
summary: Where your data lives, how to back it up, and what the Purge button does.
content:
PlanetMusic doesn't use cloud servers, so your library lives in your own browser, on your own device. That keeps it private, but it also means backing it up is up to you.

---

## 1. Where your data lives

Your data is saved in two separate places in your browser:

* **Text and settings:** Your song info, lyrics, timestamps, and app settings live in one place. It's very fast, but the space is limited.
* **Audio files:** When you upload a local MP3 to play a song, it goes into a separate, larger place built for big files. Keeping audio apart from the text is what stops your browser from crashing when you load a massive library.

Because everything is on your device, your library won't follow you to a new computer on its own. Clearing your browser data will also remove it, so keep a backup.

## 2. Exporting JSON backups

Backups matter. There's a Download icon in the top right corner of the navigation bar.

Click it and you get a `PlanetMusic_Backup.json` file with all of your Vault's text data (lyrics, timings, settings).

> **WARNING:** The JSON backup does *not* include your local MP3 files or your Deezer ARL token. If you move to a new computer, you'll need to re-upload your MP3s and re-enter your ARL.

## 3. The Purge button

If you ever want to wipe the app from your device completely, go to **Settings** and click the big red **Purge All Local Data** button.

It permanently deletes both places: your text data and your uploaded audio files. Then it resets the app. It does automatically download a JSON backup right before deleting, in case you change your mind.

title: The Live Equalizer
summary: What the pulsing bars at the bottom of the lyrics screen are, how they react to your music, and how to turn them off.
content:
If you play a local MP3 or a Deezer stream, you'll notice pulsing white bars at the bottom of the lyrics screen. That's the Live Equalizer.

---

## 1. How it works

These bars aren't a canned animation. They react to the music as it plays.

PlanetMusic listens to the sound and splits it up by pitch, from low to high. Each bar stands for one part of that range, and it rises and falls with how strong that part of the sound is. The loudest low-end hits are exaggerated a little, so the bass really stands out.

> **NOTE ON YOUTUBE:** You won't see the equalizer when you play YouTube sources. YouTube plays its audio inside its own locked-down player, and browsers don't let other sites listen in on audio from a player like that. It's a security rule that keeps sites from grabbing data they shouldn't, so there's nothing for the bars to react to.

## 2. Turning it off

If you find the equalizer distracting, or it's draining your laptop's battery, go to the **Settings** tab and turn on **Disable Animations**. The equalizer stops working while that setting is on.

title: Troubleshooting Playback & Missing Artworks
summary: Fixes for missing artist images, Deezer audio that keeps buffering, and empty search results.
content:
Here are some common problems and how to fix them.

---

## 1. Missing artist images

Sometimes an artist image loads as a broken image or a gray placeholder. That usually means the website hosting the image doesn't allow it to be shown in PlanetMusic.

* **The fix:** Click **Manage Artists** on the song panel and paste a different image URL, ideally from a site that allows it, like Wikipedia or Imgur.

Album covers can't be changed in PlanetMusic. Only artist images can.

## 2. Deezer buffering loops

If you've entered a Deezer ARL but the audio just spins and says "Buffering stream" forever, check these:

* Your ARL token may have expired. They usually last a few months.
* You might have copied the wrong cookie. Make sure it's the cookie named exactly `arl`.
* Go to Settings, paste a fresh ARL, and click **Verify Token Status**.

## 3. Empty search results

If Cosmos search finds nothing for a very famous song, Apple's search might just be confused by the way the title is written.

* **The fix:** Search with just the artist name, or remove terms like "(Remastered)" or "(feat. XYZ)" from your query.

title: Creating Custom Blogs & Workspaces
summary: How to write your own Markdown blog posts, and a quick tour of the workspaces.
content:
PlanetMusic isn't only for music. It also has a full Markdown blog editor, so you can write down your translation notes, syncing strategies, or just personal thoughts.

---

## 1. The Creator Studio

Go to the **Blog** tab and click the `+` button to open the Creator Studio. You can draft articles here in standard Markdown, and headers, lists, and bold text render as you type.

* **Title, Category & Tags:** Give your post a title, and choose whatever category and tags you like.
* **Markdown:** Standard formatting works, like `**bold**`, `_italics_`, or blockquotes with `> `.
* **Live Preview:** The right side of the screen updates in real time as you type.

> **PRO TIP:** The toolbar buttons insert Markdown syntax for you, so you don't have to type it out.

## 2. The workspaces

PlanetMusic is built from a set of workspaces:

* **Lyrics Editor:** Raw text editing and metadata entry.
* **Translation Workspace:** Phonetic transliterations and translations.
* **Sync Workspace:** Mapping timestamps to audio.
* **Image Manager:** Assigning HD images to specific artists across your Vault.

Save your work before you close a workspace. The app usually warns you if you have unsaved changes, but hitting that save button is still a good habit.

title: Importing & Exporting Translations (.TXT)
summary: How to import your own translation file into the workspace instead of using automatic translations.
content:
Sometimes you'd rather not use the automatic translations at all. Maybe you found a great translation online, or you're fluent and wrote your own in a text editor. Either way, you can load it straight into the app.

---

## 1. Exporting the template

In the Translation Workspace, click **Export Text**. It downloads a `.txt` file with your original lyrics, broken down block by block.

Each block is separated by a blank line.

## 2. Formatting the text file

Open the `.txt` file in any text editor. PlanetMusic tells the blocks apart by those blank lines, so keep them.

A well-formatted block looks like this:

```text
[lang: ja]
君の声が聞こえる
Kimi no koe ga kikoeru
I can hear your voice
```

From top to bottom, a block has:

1. **The language tag (optional):** Wrapped in brackets.
2. **The original lyric.**
3. **The phonetic transliteration (optional).**
4. **The English translation.**

If you don't need a pronunciation line, just put the translation directly under the original lyric.

## 3. Importing back into the app

When you're done editing your `.txt` file, click **Import Text** in the Translation Workspace.

PlanetMusic reads your file, matches the original lyrics to the rows on your screen, and fills in all the text boxes with your custom data. If a lyric doesn't match, it falls back to the block's position, so keep your blocks in order. Hit **Save Changes** and you're done.

title: Ambient Mode: Floating Lyrics Canvas
summary: Turn your screen into a floating lyric waterfall with Ambient Mode.
content:
Sometimes you just want to put on a playlist and zone out without staring at a grid of album covers.

That's why I built **Ambient Mode**.

---

## 1. Entering Ambient Mode

Go to the **Settings** tab and click **Enter Ambient View**.

The whole dashboard (the search bar, the song cards, the categories) disappears. All that's left is the dynamic background and the player controls at the bottom of the screen.

## 2. The lyric waterfall

While Ambient Mode is on, the app quietly looks through your whole Vault in the background and picks random synced lyric fragments and ad-libs from your songs.

Those fragments show up at the bottom of the screen as chat bubbles that float upward, with the artist's profile picture next to the lyric and its translation.

It makes a good screensaver for a second monitor or a TV.

title: Mobile Optimization: PlanetMusic on the Go
summary: How the interface and workspaces adapt to fit your phone.
content:
Using the studio on your phone? You might expect an app with syncing and translation tools to struggle on a small screen. The workspaces are built so that everything runs smoothly anyway.

---

## 1. The fluid song modal

On desktop, a song opens in a split-screen layout, with the album art on the left and the lyrics on the right.

On mobile, the modal stacks everything into a single vertical scrolling column. The album art and controls stay stuck to the top, and the lyrics fill the rest of the space below.

## 2. Workspaces on a small screen

The complex grid layouts in the Translation Workspace and Creator Studio collapse into single-column rows that are easy to read.

Even the Sync Workspace, with its dense matrix of timing buttons, rearranges itself. The keyboard emulation buttons let you tap the up and down arrows with your thumbs just as easily as hitting the spacebar on a laptop.

Wherever you are, your whole Vault goes with you.

title: How to Contact Us & Get Support
summary: Having trouble with your Vault or found a bug? Here's how to reach me.
content:
Have a question, feedback, or a bug report? The Contact tab is your direct line to me.

---

## 1. Sending a message

Go to the **Contact** tab in the main navigation bar. There's a simple form where you can type out your issue.

It's just me behind this app, and I read every message that comes through so I can keep improving it.

## 2. If you want a reply

I have a zero-tracking policy and respect your privacy, so the contact form doesn't make you enter an email address.

Here's the catch: **if you want me to get back to you, put your email address in the message itself.**

Messages come in every week, and if you ask a question without leaving any contact info, I have no way to send you an answer.

Please be specific in your message, and I'll get back to you as soon as I can.

title: Group Chat: A New Way to Experience Synced Lyrics
summary: Turn synced lyrics into a live group conversation, with artist colors, presence, and clickable lines.
content:
Lyrics don't have to feel like a block of text on a screen. I built **Group Chat View** to make synced lyrics feel more like a conversation between the artists.

---

## 1. Switching to Group Chat View

Open a song with synced lyrics and find **Lyrics View Modes** in the song panel. Select **Group Chat**, alongside Live, Focused, and Plain Text.

Each lyric appears as a message bubble, arranged into a conversation as the song plays. The active line gets a highlight, and you can click any lyric bubble to jump to that point in the track.

## 2. Follow who's singing

When the lyrics have singer information, each artist gets their own color and position in the chat. Artist avatars show who's currently active, while join and leave notices mark when they enter or exit the conversation.

For split lyrics and ad-libs, each timed part can appear as its own message, so background vocals have room in the conversation too.

## 3. A conversation that follows the music

The chat follows the song's timing. You'll see the lyric history build as the track plays, and artists can appear as typing shortly before their next line. The message timestamps follow playback as well.

> **TIP:** Group Chat View works best with synced lyrics and singer assignments. Use the Sync Workspace to add timing, then check the singer tags in the lyrics so each message can be attributed to the right artist.
